card.title: Fine, What’s the Process?
card.instruction: Accept any strange custom or institution as real, then focus on deadlines, permissions, responsibilities, and what happens when someone misses a step.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For tonight's moon audit, who signs the village's findings?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The oldest owl. I'm delivering them, but my shift ends at sunset.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Can we get its signature before you finish?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It starts at moonrise. I'll stay, but you have to approve my overtime.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Approved. Put 'waiting for owl' on your timesheet. Who covers delivery if it's cloudy?

mechanism: A accepts the owl-signature moon audit and turns its timing into overtime approval and delivery-cover questions.
confusable: Unlike absurd bureaucratic obstruction, A focuses on making the strange institution operational through clear responsibility and scheduling.
comparison: The audit alternative handles night shifts and weather cover; the dragon ceremony alternative handles incompatible safety practice and financial responsibility.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
